questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML = HyperText Markup Language — the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Which HTML tag creates the largest heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the largest heading. Headings go from <h1> (biggest) to <h6> (smallest).

questions.question: What does CSS stand for?
questions.explanation: CSS = Cascading Style Sheets — controls how HTML elements look (colors, fonts, layout).

questions.question: Which CSS property changes text color?
questions.explanation: The 'color' property changes text color. Example: color: blue; or color: #3b82f6;

questions.question: What is the CSS Box Model order from inside to outside?
questions.explanation: Box Model (inside to outside): Content → Padding → Border → Margin.

questions.question: Which CSS display value is used for modern layouts?
questions.explanation: display: flex (Flexbox) is the modern way to create layouts — easy alignment and spacing.

questions.question: What does the <a> tag create in HTML?
questions.explanation: Link text creates a clickable hyperlink to another page or section.

questions.question: Which attribute makes an image accessible for screen readers?
questions.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides text description of an image for screen readers and when image fails to load.

questions.question: How do you select an element with class 'card' in CSS?
questions.explanation: Use a dot (.) for classes: .card { }. Use # for IDs: #card { }.

questions.question: What CSS property adds space between flex items?
questions.explanation: The 'gap' property adds space between flex items. Example: gap: 16px;

questions.question: Which unit is relative to the root font size?
questions.explanation: rem = relative to root element font size. If root = 16px, then 1.5rem = 24px. Better for responsive design.

questions.question: What is the purpose of @media queries in CSS?
options: Make designs responsive for different screen sizes
questions.explanation: @media queries apply different CSS rules based on screen size — essential for responsive design.
